# 🌌 TRPOLARIS Control Center v1.8.0

**Signed Update Engine · Stable/Beta Channels · Native Updater · Shorter App Identity**

TRPOLARIS Control Center v1.8.0 introduces a redesigned application update system. Release metadata is read from the GitHub Releases API, manifests are digitally signed, packages are verified before installation, and the EXE is replaced by a native C# helper without creating a backup copy.

[⬇️ Download Release](https://github.com/trpolaris/TRPOLARIS-NFSU2-Web-Control-Center/releases/latest) · [📦 Source Code](https://github.com/trpolaris/TRPOLARIS-NFSU2-Web-Control-Center) · [🛠️ Report an Issue](https://github.com/trpolaris/TRPOLARIS-NFSU2-Web-Control-Center/issues)

</div>

---

## ✨ What's New in v1.8.0

### 🔐 Signed Update Manifests

- GitHub Releases API is the source of release metadata; a standalone `version.txt` is not used to trigger updates.
- `update-manifest.json` is signed with RSA-SHA256.
- The application contains the trusted public key and verifies the signature before accepting a release.
- The downloaded executable is verified using its exact size and SHA-256 hash.
- Release tag, SemVer version, platform, channel, asset name and minimum supported version are checked against the signed manifest.

### 🚦 Stable and Beta Channels

- Stable channel lists published stable releases only.
- Beta channel includes prereleases and stable releases, ordered using SemVer precedence.
- The Update Preferences window lets users choose the release channel.
- Startup checks can run every launch, daily, or only when manually requested.

### ⚡ Efficient Release Checks and Downloads

- ETag / HTTP 304 caching reduces repeated GitHub API payload transfers.
- Interrupted executable downloads can resume using HTTP Range requests.
- Package size and hash are checked before installation.
- The last 30 update outcomes are stored locally and shown in Update Preferences.

### 🧩 Native C# Update Host

- The PowerShell-based application updater has been removed.
- A temporary copy of the running application acts as a native helper process.
- The verified executable is staged on the target volume and moved into place after the main process exits.
- A startup health marker confirms that the updated application opened.
- No `.previous`, `.bak`, or other application backup copy is created during updates.
- Because backups are intentionally disabled, a post-replacement startup failure is logged but cannot automatically restore the previous EXE.

### 🏷️ Shorter Product Identity

- Product name: **TRPOLARIS Control Center**
- New executable: `TRPOLARIS.ControlCenter.exe`
- Assembly, file and informational versions are generated from the project version.
- Existing v1.7.3 installations remain compatible through a legacy-named transition asset and `latest.json`; the new application migrates itself to the shorter executable name on first launch.

### 🐳 Installer and WSL/Docker Reliability

- The first-run Docker Desktop – Ubuntu WSL Integration readiness check continues retrying when the Docker CLI is not yet available.
- PowerShell 5.1 native stderr handling no longer interrupts the Docker readiness retry loop.
- WSL user and project path detection remains dynamic across Windows drives and Linux users.

---

## 🔄 Release Assets

Each v1.8.0 release contains:

- `TRPOLARIS.ControlCenter.exe` — current application
- `update-manifest.json` — RSA-SHA256 signed update metadata for current clients
- `TRPOLARIS.NFSU2.WebControlCenter.exe` — compatibility asset for v1.7.3 clients upgrading to v1.8.0
- `latest.json` — compatibility manifest for existing v1.7.3 clients

The private signing key is stored only in the repository's GitHub Actions secret `UPDATE_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`. It is not included in the repository or release assets.
